clue.text: One who's leaving, a man retiring before peak

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the man's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ed is a common short form of a man's name, Edward
the peak of a cap is its visor, the stiff brim at the front

explanation.surface: A man stepping down from office just short of reaching the summit of his career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns ED into DE. 'Leaving' here means leaving property by will, not departing.
explanation.definitionFit: A devisor is a legal term for a person who bequeaths property in a will, someone who passes it to heirs.

clue.text: Something that fails to impress on 5th November?

definitions.text: Something that fails to impress on 5th November?

parts.words: Something that fails to impress on 5th November?
parts.note: Bonfire Night in Britain is marked with fireworks, and a wet firework fizzles out instead of going bang

explanation.surface: A disappointing firework on Guy Fawkes Night.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 November is Bonfire Night in Britain, celebrated with fireworks; a squib is a small firecracker.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an anticlimax comes from a wet firecracker that fails to explode.

clue.text: Brave man following unqualified driver in a tank

indicators.note: in means the driver and the man go inside the tank

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids

indicators.note: following means the man comes after the driver

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British car driven by someone without a licence
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A soldier rides behind a learner at the controls of an armoured vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Valiant and brave both describe someone courageous in the face of danger.

clue.text: Tip appearing in paper — cash laid out

indicators.note: laid out means spread and arranged afresh, so the letters of paper and cash are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports that money has been spent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid out' rearranges PAPERCASH. A tip in Britain is a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip, in British English, is a dump where junk and rubbish are thrown.

clue.text: Flower came up

explanation.surface: A bloom that sprouted.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose is a thorny garden bloom; the past tense of rise means ascended.

clue.text: Calm sea

explanation.surface: A peaceful stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means peaceful and tranquil, and it is also the name of the largest ocean on Earth.

clue.text: Senior member of the House, a Conservative, precluding debate

parts.note: père, French for father, follows a name to mean the senior, as in Dumas père
MP is a Member of Parliament, sitting in the House of Commons
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An elder Tory MP shuts down discussion in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senior member of the House' wants to be one person; it is PERE plus MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt order that allows no argument or discussion is called this.

clue.text: Company were not wholly taken with shrink

indicators.note: not wholly means the word were loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A firm's staff were partly won over by a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not wholly' cuts were to WER. 'shrink' is a verb here, not slang for a psychiatrist.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch or recoil in fear, to shrink away.

clue.text: Two women between them run the state

indicators.note: between them means the letter goes between the two names

parts.note: Flo is a woman's name, short for Florence
Ida is another woman's name
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A pair of women jointly govern an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for run in cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida is one of the fifty US states, in the far south-east.

clue.text: Bring forth young student hiding in hollow

indicators.note: hiding in means one letter is concealed inside the other word

parts.note: a cave is a hollow in rock
L for learner, a student

explanation.surface: A pupil conceals himself in a cave to give birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows, whales and elephants calve when they give birth to their offspring.

clue.text: Racer who suffers a setback during the preliminaries

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the letters found are read in reverse
during means the letters sit inside the word preliminaries

explanation.surface: An athlete stumbles in the heats before the main race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' picks RELIM out of preliminaries; 'suffers a setback' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner or horse that specialises in races over one mile is an example of a racer.

clue.text: The way an experienced head takes an opinion survey

definitions.text: The way an experienced head takes an opinion survey

parts.words: The way an experienced head takes an opinion survey
parts.note: a straw in the wind shows the way it blows, and a poll is a head, so a wise old head tests opinion by a rough informal vote

explanation.surface: A seasoned headteacher's method of sounding out the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on 'straws in the wind' showing which way opinion blows, and on POLL as an old word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An unofficial show of hands taken to gauge feeling is an informal survey of opinion.

clue.text: Rogue I found in Dublin Bay

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous rascal or rogue

explanation.surface: A fugitive confesses he turned up on the Irish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Dublin Bay prawns are the langoustines sold as this dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin Bay prawns, or langoustines, are what is breaded and fried under this name.

clue.text: Write off to a miser in need of reform

indicators.note: needing reform means needing to be reshaped, so the letters of to a miser are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tightfisted man is told his bad debts should be cleared from the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of reform' rearranges TOAMISER.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay off or reduce a debt or the value of an asset gradually is to write it off over time.

clue.text: Advisable, and fair too.

parts.note: just means fair or impartial
as well means also or too

explanation.surface: A recommendation that is both sensible and equitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it would be better to do something is saying it is advisable.

clue.text: Change from being fast and loose

explanation.surface: Converting from a fixed state to a slack one.
explanation.definitionFit: Undoing a knot changes something tied fast into something free, and to loose a rope is to undo it.

clue.text: Where climbers go mad

explanation.surface: Mountaineers losing their minds.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbing plants or climbers scale a vertical surface, and the idiom means furious or crazy.

clue.text: Confidentially. Reno usen't to be liberal

indicators.note: liberal means free, so the letters of Reno usen't are freed into a new order

explanation.surface: A secret: the city of Reno was never broadminded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be liberal' rearranges RENOUSENT; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means between ourselves, said privately or in confidence.

clue.text: Exponent producing record with a noisy beat

parts.note: a log is a written record, such as a ship's log

indicators.note: noisy signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: rhythm is a regular beat in music

explanation.surface: A performer making a recording with a loud drum track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exponent' suggests a performer; it is the mathematical term. 'noisy' gives RITHM from the sound of rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics, a logarithm is the exponent or power to which a base must be raised to give a number.

clue.text: Athlete safe to give signal to start sailing

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A sportsman is trusted to give the go-ahead for a regatta.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxbridge sporting honour; PETER is safe-crackers' slang. The flag is hoisted when a ship is about to leave port.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue and white flag flown by a ship about to leave harbour is a nautical departure signal.

clue.text: Ignorant girl is given pottery

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
ware means pottery, as in earthenware

explanation.surface: A naive young woman receives a gift of ceramics.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no knowledge of a matter is ignorant of it.

clue.text: Object primarily to having inquisitive neighbours gawping

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone protests at nosy people next door staring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb, as in protest, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Any item or article can be called an object.

clue.text: Bury for instance housed a number

indicators.note: housed means one part is put inside another as if given a home

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: The Lancashire town of Bury, for example, contained a certain population.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital B makes Bury look like the English town; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number with no fractional part is called an integer.

clue.text: This case is incorrect? Correct!

indicators.note: being incorrect means being wrong, so the letters of this case are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A teacher marks a legal case wrong and orders it put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is incorrect' rearranges THISCASE. 'Correct' is a verb meaning to punish, not 'put right'.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct someone, in the old sense, is to punish or rebuke them.

clue.text: Effective under 100 or 200 yards …

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below the other part

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
able means capable or effective

explanation.surface: Something works best below a certain distance on the range.
explanation.walkthrough: A cable is a nautical measure of about 200 yards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable's length is a nautical unit of roughly 200 yards, a tenth of a sea mile.

clue.text: - perfunctory but satisfactory within ten

indicators.note: within means put inside the word ten

parts.note: OK means satisfactory or acceptable

explanation.surface: A half-hearted effort that still passes muster in ten marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A token gesture is done for form's sake only, perfunctory.

clue.text: One who puts up an uncouth fellow without taste, outwardly

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the rough fellow surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a bear is a rough, ill-mannered person

indicators.note: outwardly means only the outside letters of taste are used

explanation.surface: A host tolerates a boor who lacks refinement on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside'. On a shoot, beaters drive game birds up into the air, and that is what 'puts up' means, not 'tolerates'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a shoot, a beater flushes or rouses game birds into the air for the guns.

clue.text: Shock when daring exploit is not fully achieved

indicators.note: not fully achieved means the word is left one letter short of completion

parts.note: a stunt is a daring feat

explanation.surface: A daredevil feat falls short and startles everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is not fully achieved' drops the last T of STUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or daze them.

clue.text: Symbol of ability to fight using deadly punch

parts.note: black can mean deadly or sinister, as in the Black Death
to belt someone is to punch them hard

explanation.surface: A martial arts expert proves himself with a lethal blow.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest grade in judo or karate is marked by a sash of this colour, showing fighting mastery.

clue.text: Should anything …

explanation.surface: Should anything change, the next clue continues.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a modal verb of obligation, and is also an old spelling of aught, meaning anything at all.

clue.text: … change, ten pounds are unchangeable

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of these letters

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Even if things shift, a tenner stays the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges TEN, L and ARE. The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue's surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting never alters, so it is unchangeable.

clue.text: Patent medicine in no way unusual

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
rum is British slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A branded remedy that is perfectly ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old-fashioned British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack remedy or cure-all sold under a brand is a patent medicine.
